name: Bienal de Cuenca
funding: Run by the Fundación Municipal Bienal de Cuenca, a city body. The 17th edition cost about $1.2M, from municipal money, private-company agreements and self-raised funds.

name: Museo Antropológico y de Arte Contemporáneo (MAAC)
funding: Ecuador's Culture vice-ministry (merged into Education in 2025) runs and funds it on a budget above USD 2.5M, and pays the city's Malecón 2000 foundation near USD 500,000 a year.

name: Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito
funding: Run by the Fundación Museos de la Ciudad, a nonprofit acting on commission of the Quito municipality. Admission is free.

name: Museo Nacional del Ecuador (MuNa)
funding: State national museum; the government has budgeted about US$100M for a new building, with a state-owned enterprise managing construction.

name: Contemporary Image Collective
funding: No funder list is published. The Arab Fund for Arts and Culture lists a 2024 CiC project under Egypt's National Cultural Opportunities Fund. Cairo artists depend on foreign grants.

name: Darb 1718 Contemporary Art and Culture Center
funding: Small non-profit mainly funded by artist Moataz Nasr. 2022 Moleskine Foundation grant. 2025 artist-donated auction at Tarathuna.

name: Medrar for Contemporary Art
funding: Space set up with support from Young Arab Theatre Fund, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Abbara, Roberto Cimetta Fund, Netherlands Embassy in Cairo and AFAC through a Swiss SDC grant.

name: Museum of Modern Egyptian Art
funding: Owned by the Ministry of Culture.

name: Townhouse Gallery
funding: Small independent non-profit founded 1998 by William Wells, now a foundation; no funder list found and its website no longer resolves.

name: Art D'Égypte
funding: Private firm of Nadine Abdel Ghaffar. Egypt's foreign and tourism ministries and UNESCO sponsor Forever Is Now. Partners: LMD, Suez Canal Bank, BMW (2026); TotalEnergies, Afreximbank (2024).

name: Museo de Arte de El Salvador (MARTE)
Museo de la Palabra y la Imagen (MUPI)
funding: Private non-profit. AGIAMONDO and the Ford Foundation backed its 2026 archive move; gifts from citizens, the diaspora and firms repay the annexe mortgage. Its site lists no donors or budget.
